requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1.
requirements.summary: vg_srvdata/lv_data was created, formatted as XFS, and mounted read-write at /srv/data. The final post-restart observation shows the active 2.00 GiB LV and recovered mount.

requirements.requirement: Grow the logical volume to at least 2 GB while it remains mounted and preserve its contents.
requirements.summary: Direct before-and-after evidence shows online growth from 1.00 GiB to 2.00 GiB, the same mount ID throughout, successful XFS growth, and an unchanged content hash. The recovered filesystem reports 2,080,374,784 bytes and retains the original content after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 are identical before the work and after restart. The existing platform LVM, XFS, loop-device, and systemd tooling completed the implementation successfully without package changes.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. The evidence directly demonstrates creation and mounting of the logical volume, uninterrupted online growth to 2.00 GiB with content integrity, retention of the installed OS and kernel, and persistence across a completed node restart. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement and observed disconnect, changed boot identity, and recovered read-write storage are all captured and independently corroborated by lifecycle boot identities.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed state-changing commands had a clear role in creating, growing, persisting, verifying, or restart-testing the requested storage. The continuity and post-restart write files were bounded functional evidence. No unnecessary mutations were identified. The unsuccessful lvmdevices option was read-only, and the connection failures occurred during the required reboot. Final observations show no failed services, new exposure, temporary-file residue beyond normal reboot-generated systemd directories, or package-health damage.
